import io, struct
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image  # Pillow wheel built with libtiff; no rasterio/GDAL/tifffile needed

def read_gfa(path, month, rows=slice(None), chunk=120):
    """Global Fire Atlas monthly GeoTIFF -> (data[lat, lon] float32 with NaN, lat, lon).
    month = 1..12 (band k = calendar month k). rows = optional raster-row slice (row 0 = 89.875N).
    Pillow refuses 12-sample TIFFs, so the LZW strips (1 row x 1440 px x 12 float32 each) are
    re-described by a synthetic IFD as a 1-band float32 image 1440*12 wide and decoded by libtiff."""
    buf = open(path, 'rb').read()
    assert buf[:4] == b'II*\x00', 'little-endian classic TIFF expected'
    off = struct.unpack_from('<I', buf, 4)[0]
    t = {}
    for i in range(struct.unpack_from('<H', buf, off)[0]):
        tag, typ, cnt, val = struct.unpack_from('<HHII', buf, off + 2 + 12 * i)
        sz = {1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 2, 4: 4, 12: 8}[typ] * cnt
        p = off + 2 + 12 * i + 8 if sz <= 4 else val
        t[tag] = buf[p:p + sz].decode().rstrip('\0') if typ == 2 else \
            struct.unpack('<' + {1: 'B', 3: 'H', 4: 'I', 12: 'd'}[typ] * cnt, buf[p:p + sz])
    W, H, S = t[256][0], t[257][0], t[277][0]                       # 1440, 720, 12
    assert (t[259][0], t[284][0], t[278][0], t.get(317, (1,))[0], set(t[258]), set(t[339])) == (5, 1, 1, 1, {32}, {3})
    idx = range(H)[rows]
    out = np.empty((len(idx), W), np.float32)
    for k in range(0, len(idx), chunk):
        r = idx[k:k + chunk]; n = len(r); b = bytearray(buf) + b'\0' * (len(buf) % 2)
        ifd = len(b); arr = ifd + 2 + 11 * 12 + 4
        so = arr if n > 1 else t[273][r[0]]; sc = arr + 4 * n if n > 1 else t[279][r[0]]
        ent = [(256, 4, 1, W * S), (257, 4, 1, n), (258, 3, 1, 32), (259, 3, 1, 5), (262, 3, 1, 1), (273, 4, n, so),
               (277, 3, 1, 1), (278, 4, 1, 1), (279, 4, n, sc), (284, 3, 1, 1), (339, 3, 1, 3)]
        b += struct.pack('<H', 11) + b''.join(struct.pack('<HHII', *e) for e in ent) + b'\0' * 4
        if n > 1:
            b += struct.pack('<%dI' % n, *[t[273][j] for j in r]) + struct.pack('<%dI' % n, *[t[279][j] for j in r])
        struct.pack_into('<I', b, 4, ifd)
        out[k:k + n] = np.asarray(Image.open(io.BytesIO(bytes(b))), np.float32).reshape(n, W, S)[:, :, month - 1]
    out[out == float(t.get(42113, '-9999'))] = np.nan                # GDAL_NODATA tag = "-9999"
    (dx, dy), (x0, y0) = t[33550][:2], t[33922][3:5]                # 0.25, 0.25 ; -180, 90 = top-left corner
    lon = x0 + dx * (np.arange(W) + 0.5)                            # -179.875 .. 179.875 (west -> east)
    lat = y0 - dy * (np.asarray(idx) + 0.5)                         # 89.875 .. -89.875 (north -> south)
    return out, lat, lon

if __name__ == '__main__':
    a, lat, lon = read_gfa('/home/sawy3/nasa_work/data/raw/global_fire_atlas/Global_fire_atlas_ignitions_monthly_2003.tif', month=1)
    print(a.shape, lat[0], lat[-1], lon[0], lon[-1], np.isfinite(a).sum(), np.nanmean(a), np.nansum(a))
# tested output: (720, 1440) 89.875 -89.875 -179.875 179.875 11366 7.8334765 89035.3   (0.35 s, 71 MB peak RSS)
# rows=slice(312, 408) decodes only 11.875N..-11.875S (SE Asia band). Works for all 7 variables (same layout).
# 18/18 test cases bit-identical to the cross-checked decoder.

specs.use_for_fire_harmony: Only covers 2003-2016, so it cannot be a live input. What it gives per H3 hexagon (the project's level 5, about 253 km2) and calendar month: (1) VALIDATION, the main use. It is an independent count of individual fires (ignitions) and a burned-area estimate (ignitions x size, km2). These test whether the harmonized monthly FIRMS counts follow real fires and burned area, as the architecture doc plans. They can also calibrate hotspots-per-fire and hotspots-per-km2-burned by region, land cover and peat. The VIIRS S-NPP versus MODIS comparison is only possible for 2012-2016. (2) DRIVERS and fire-regime descriptors: ignitions-weighted mean fire size, duration, speed, daily expansion and fire line per hexagon, as monthly values or a 2003-2016 climatology. These separate long, large peat and forest fires (big haze sources) from short, small savanna and cropland burns, and can be related to GFWED FWI, IMERG rain, MERRA-2 weather and ONI/DMI. (3) HAZE: fire size, duration and spread in SE Asia as covariates for MERRA-2 CNN PM2.5 in 2003-2016 (for example the 2006 and 2015 El Nino years). (4) OUTLOOK: seasonal baseline and training targets for 2003-2016 only. direction has little use (categorical, biased toward cardinal directions). Aggregation rules: a 0.25 deg cell (773 km2 at the equator, 385 km2 at 60N) covers about 1.5-3 level-5 hexagons, so split cells by overlap area. Sum ignitions and burned area as area-weighted totals after setting NaN to 0 on land. Average size, duration, speed, spread and fire_line as sum(w*ign*var)/sum(w*ign), with w the overlap fraction. Use an ignitions-weighted mode for direction. Note GFA uses calendar months by burn date, while the gold layer uses solar months.

specs.grid: All six products use the same MODIS land sinusoidal grid. StructMetadata gives Projection GCTP_SNSOID / HE5_GCTP_SNSOID, sphere radius R = 6371007.181 m, GridOrigin UL. The UpperLeftPointMtrs of MODIS and VIIRS files agree to 5 micrometres. The global grid is 36 x 18 tiles. A tile is T = 1111950.519667 m square (10 degrees of arc at the equator). The UL corner of tile hHvV is x = -20015109.354 + H*T, y = 10007554.677 - V*T; for h08v05 the stored UL is (-11119505.196662, 4447802.078664) and LR is (-10007554.676995, 3335851.558997). Fire maps: 1200 x 1200 per tile, pixel 926.625433 m, area 0.858635 km2. Burned area: 2400 x 2400 per tile, pixel 463.312717 m, area 0.214659 km2. The grid is equal-area, so every pixel has the same area. Arrays are [row, col] = [YDim, XDim] (MOD/MYD14A1: [day, YDim, XDim]); row 0 is the north edge (north to south), col 0 is the west edge. This was verified: FIRMS Aqua points land 100% on MYD14A1 fire pixels, and flipping rows or columns drops that to 0.1%. A given (row, col) is the same place in all four fire maps; 500 m pixel (r, c) nests in 1 km pixel (r//2, c//2) (the 1 km centre equals the mean of its 2x2 500 m centres to 1e-8 deg). Pixel centre with s = T/n: x = X0 + H*T + (col+0.5)*s; y = Y0 - V*T - (row+0.5)*s; lat = deg(y/R); lon = deg(x / (R*cos(lat_rad))). So lat is 1D (one value per row) but lon is 2D (it depends on row and col). Inverse: x = R*lon_rad*cos(lat_rad), y = R*lat_rad, H = floor((x-X0)/T), V = floor((Y0-y)/T), col = floor((x-X0-H*T)/s), row = floor((Y0-y-V*T)/s). Longitudes are -180..180, and none of the 10 tiles has off-globe pixels. VIIRS files also store XDim/YDim in metres, but these are pixel upper-left edges, not centres: XDim[0] is exactly the UL x and steps by 926.625433, so add +463.3127 to x and -463.3127 to y to get centres. Tile extents (1 km pixel centres): h08v05 30-40N, 130.5W-103.9W; h11v03 50-60N, 140.0W-93.4W; h12v10 10-20S, 63.8W-50.8W; h12v11 20-30S, 69.3W-53.2W; h20v08 0-10N, 20.0E-30.5E; h20v10 10-20S, 20.3E-31.9E; h22v02 60-70N, 80.0E-146.2E; h25v06 20-30N, 74.5E-92.4E; h29v09 0-10S, 110.0E-121.9E; h30v10 10-20S, 121.9E-138.3E.
quirks: The last MODIS file of the year (MOD14A1/MYD14A1 A2019361) covers 2019-12-27..2020-01-03. For 2019 only, drop layers 5-7 of that file. Always take dates from the 'Dates' attribute, not from filename DOY + index across years.

VNP14A1 and VJ114A1 come from the 750 m M-band VIIRS fire product, not the 375 m I-band product in FIRMS. Evidence: the 'sample' valid_range is 0-3199, which fits the 3200-sample M-band swath. On h20v10 2019-08-30 only 34.3% of the 8,742 FIRMS Suomi-NPP 375 m points fall on a VNP14A1 fire pixel (57.4% within 1 px), while FIRMS MODIS points match the MODIS grids 99.9-100%. So the 3.4x-8.1x 'VIIRS / MODIS' ratios in the Acquisition Log (from 375 m FIRMS) do not describe these grids.

MODIS grids flag more 1 km cells than there are swath detections. On h20v10 2019-08-30 MYD14A1 has 3,035 fire cells for 1,328 FIRMS Aqua points (MOD14A1 1,751 cells for 1,042 Terra points). Only 42.4% of grid fire cells contain a point, but 98.4% are within 1 px and 99.6% within 2 px. This fits large off-nadir swath footprints being written into several grid cells (an inference, not a documented fact). Grid fire-pixel counts are therefore not detection counts, and per-pixel MODIS-vs-VIIRS matching needs a neighbourhood tolerance or aggregation to H3.

MODIS has orbit gaps at low latitudes, stored as class 0. MOD14A1 h20v10 has about 167,000 px (11.6%) missing on 4 of 8 days; MYD14A1 2019-08-30 has 52,854 px missing; h08v05 had none. The 6 sampled VIIRS tile-days had no class 0. Leave class 0 (and cloud, class 4) out of the denominator.

Each daily layer merges the day and night overpasses of that UTC day. MOD14A1 CoreMetadata lists 8 MOD14GD + 8 MOD14GN input granules with DAYNIGHTFLAG 'Both'; VIIRS InputPointer lists VNP14GD + VNP14GN. The only time-of-day information in the files is QA bit 2 (day/night); there are no overpass times.
Sinusoidal grid: lat is 1D per row but lon is 2D. The reader returns lat1d with shape (n,) and lon2d with shape (n, n); a true 1D lon does not exist.

FireMask _FillValue = 0 is declared only in the MODIS files; VIIRS has no _FillValue (0 still means missing input). Classes 1 and 2 never appeared in the samples. Class 6 'unknown' does appear (MOD14A1 h30v10 2019-12-31: 2,515 px; VNP14A1 same day: 37 px).
MODIS QA has no legend attribute (VIIRS QA does). VNP64A1 has no 'QA Legend' attribute (MCD64A1 does).

Burn Date in each monthly file only holds burns within that calendar month; combine the 12 files for an annual map (their DOY ranges do not overlap). -1 = unmapped, -2 = water, 0 = unburned. 'First Day'/'Last Day' are the detection window and run about 3 weeks past the month.

xarray can open the VIIRS HDF5 group, but no coordinates attach (XDim/YDim live in the parent group), and FireMask stays raw uint8. h5py returns string attributes as bytes (e.g. b'2019-08-30 00:00:00'), so decode them. HDF4 files need pyhdf.

VNP64A1 has the misspelled global attribute 'VERITICALTILENUMBER'. Take the tile from the filename or the 'tile' attribute. The burned-area grid names also differ (MOD_Grid_Monthly_500m_DB_BA vs MOD_Grid_Monthly_500m_BA).

Per-file summary attributes match the arrays exactly and allow screening without reading data: MODIS FirePix (8 values, one per day) equals the count of classes 7-9 (plus CloudPix, MissingPix, UnknownPix); VIIRS FireCells (in /HDFEOS/ADDITIONAL/FILE_ATTRIBUTES) equals the count of classes 7-9; burned-area BurnedCells equals the count of Burn Date > 0 (also MissingCells, LandCells, ValidLandCells).

h29v09 is 0-10S, 110-121.9E: southern Kalimantan, Java east of 110E, Bali and Nusa Tenggara, SW Sulawesi. It contains no part of Sumatra (95-106E), although the Acquisition Log labels it 'Sumatra / Borneo'. 3N 101E is in tile h28v08, which was not downloaded.

On the one sampled tile-day, Aqua agrees with VIIRS about 3x more often than Terra. That fits Aqua sharing the afternoon/after-midnight orbit times of S-NPP and NOAA-20 (orbit times are general knowledge, not in the files). Compute the MODIS-sees-VIIRS probability separately for Terra and Aqua.

pyproj, rasterio and h3 are not installed in /home/sawy3/nasa_work/fire-harmony/.venv; the reader uses the closed-form spherical formula. DuckDB's spatial extension is also absent: FIRMS geometry must be cast to BLOB and the 21-byte WKB points parsed by hand (done in /tmp/fhinspect/geocheck.py).
Small VIIRS files (about 117 KB, mostly h30v10 in the dry season) are low-entropy clear tiles, not empty files. I did not open all 3,650 files per product to check for empty days.

import re
import numpy as np

R = 6371007.181                       # sphere radius (m), ProjParams in StructMetadata
T = 1111950.519667                    # tile width = height (m) = 10 deg of arc at the equator
X0, Y0 = -20015109.354, 10007554.677  # upper-left corner of tile h00v00 (m); 36 x 18 tiles


def tile_latlon(h, v, n):
    """Pixel-CENTRE lat (1D, one per row, north->south) and lon (2D, row x col), degrees.
    n = 1200 for the 1 km fire maps, 2400 for the 500 m burned area."""
    s = T / n                                         # 926.625433 m or 463.312717 m
    x = X0 + h * T + (np.arange(n) + 0.5) * s
    y = Y0 - v * T - (np.arange(n) + 0.5) * s
    lat = np.degrees(y / R)
    lon = np.degrees(x[None, :] / (R * np.cos(np.radians(lat))[:, None]))
    return lat, lon


def latlon_to_tile(lat, lon, n):
    """Inverse: lat/lon (deg) -> (h, v, row, col) on the n x n per-tile grid."""
    s = T / n
    x = R * np.radians(lon) * np.cos(np.radians(lat))
    y = R * np.radians(lat)
    h = np.floor((x - X0) / T).astype(int)
    v = np.floor((Y0 - y) / T).astype(int)
    return h, v, np.floor((Y0 - y - v * T) / s).astype(int), np.floor((x - X0 - h * T) / s).astype(int)


def read_tile(path, day=0):
    """-> (data2d float32, lat1d, lon2d, date).
    Fire maps: FireMask class 1-9, 0 'missing input data' -> NaN.
      MOD14A1/MYD14A1: day = layer 0..7 of the 8-day stack; VNP14A1/VJ114A1: 1 day per file.
    Burned area (MCD64A1/VNP64A1): Burn Date day-of-year 1-366, 0 = unburned;
      -1 unmapped and -2 water -> NaN."""
    name = path.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]
    prod = name.split('.')[0]
    h, v = map(int, re.search(r'\.h(\d\d)v(\d\d)\.', name).groups())
    if prod in ('VNP14A1', 'VJ114A1'):                         # HDF5 (h5py)
        import h5py
        with h5py.File(path, 'r') as f:
            a = f['HDFEOS/GRIDS/VIIRS_Grid_Daily_Fire/Data Fields/FireMask'][:].astype(np.float32)
            date = f.attrs['RangeBeginningDate']
        date = date.decode() if isinstance(date, bytes) else str(date)
        a[a == 0] = np.nan
    else:                                                      # HDF4 (pyhdf)
        from pyhdf.SD import SD, SDC
        sd = SD(path, SDC.READ)
        ga = sd.attributes()
        if prod in ('MOD14A1', 'MYD14A1'):
            a = sd.select('FireMask')[day, :, :].astype(np.float32)   # reads one day only
            date = ga['Dates'].split()[day]
            a[a == 0] = np.nan
        else:                                                  # MCD64A1, VNP64A1
            a = sd.select('Burn Date')[:, :].astype(np.float32)
            date = '%d DOY %03d-%03d' % (ga['year'], ga['ProductStartDay'], ga['ProductEndDay'])
            a[a < 0] = np.nan
        sd.end()
    lat, lon = tile_latlon(h, v, a.shape[0])
    return a, lat, lon, date

specs.use_for_fire_harmony: This is a calibration sample, not global coverage: 10 tiles, 2019 only, so results must carry to other areas through covariates such as region, land cover (MCD12C1) and FRP. Per H3 cell and month, built from pixel centres (tile_latlon) on the shared 1 km grid: (1) P(MODIS fire | VIIRS fire), counted separately for Terra and Aqua against S-NPP and NOAA-20, by FireMask confidence. Use same-UTC-day pairs, leave out pixels where MODIS has class 0 (gap) or 4 (cloud), and allow a 1-2 px tolerance or count per H3 cell-day, because MODIS footprints spread over neighbouring cells. (2) The reverse probability, and the ratio of fire cell-days, as harmonization factors. Note these grids give 750 m VIIRS vs 1 km MODIS behaviour; the 375 m FIRMS VIIRS needs its own step (FIRMS points can be mapped onto the same grid with latlon_to_tile, as tested). (3) Detection-limit curves: P(MODIS detects | VIIRS MaxFRP), from MaxFRP (x0.1 MW). (4) Observation-opportunity covariates: cloud (4) and missing (0) frequency per cell-month, and day/night share from QA bit 2. (5) Validation: monthly burned area per cell (count of Burn Date > 0 times 0.214659 km2) from MCD64A1 and VNP64A1, burn-date timing against active-fire dates, and burned area with no active fire (omission). Neither haze nor outlook data are in these products.
